es: Redactar un párrafo de resultados con hallazgos cuantificados, lenguaje cauto, un límite explicado y un paso siguiente, sin afirmar más de lo que los datos permiten.

teaching.en: Two findings stand out: sixty per cent of the pupils sleep under eight hours, and twice as many girls as boys feel tired.
teaching.es: Dos hallazgos destacan: el sesenta por ciento de los alumnos duerme menos de ocho horas, y el doble de chicas que de chicos se siente cansado.
teaching.explanationEs: Stand out anuncia los datos más importantes; cada hallazgo lleva una cifra concreta, no una impresión.

teaching.en: The figures indicate that tired pupils tend to score lower, although they appear to say nothing about which comes first.
teaching.es: Las cifras indican que los alumnos cansados tienden a sacar notas más bajas, aunque parecen no decir nada sobre qué va primero.
teaching.explanationEs: Indicate y appear to son verbos cautos; tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia, no una regla.

teaching.en: However, to some extent a lack of sleep may adversely affect marks, although motivation and health matter at least as much.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, hasta cierto punto la falta de sueño puede afectar negativamente a las notas, aunque la motivación y la salud importan al menos tanto.
teaching.explanationEs: To some extent limita el alcance de la afirmación; a lack of + incontable nombra la carencia.

teaching.en: However, every pupil came from one school, so these findings should be read with caution until they are repeated elsewhere.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, todos los alumnos procedían de una sola escuela, así que estos hallazgos deben leerse con cautela hasta que se repitan en otro lugar.
teaching.explanationEs: However abre el límite del estudio; with caution es la conclusión práctica para el lector.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que interpreta los datos con la cautela adecuada.

choices.text: Short sleep seems linked to tiredness; the cause is unclear.
Short sleep clearly causes tiredness, so schools must act.
Tiredness makes pupils sleep less, and the figures prove it.

feedback.es: Sin seguimiento en el tiempo solo se puede hablar de una relación; las otras frases afirman una causa que los datos no establecen.

hint.es: Busca el verbo cauto y fíjate en que la causa queda abierta.

origin.text: Data: among forty pupils who sleep little, thirty feel tired; among forty who sleep well, ten feel tired. No pupil was followed over time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una falta de sueño puede afectar a sus notas.»

feedback.es: A lack of + incontable expresa una carencia; a shortage of es sinónimo.

hint.es: Sustantivo de cuatro letras: lo contrario de «tener suficiente».

origin.text: Pupils who sleep badly are often tired in class, so a ___ of sleep may well affect their marks.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Haría falta más investigación con una muestra mayor antes de generalizar.»

answer.text: Further research with a larger sample is needed before we generalise

feedback.es: Further research + is needed cierra el informe; before we generalise indica el objetivo del paso siguiente.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto: la investigación.

prompt.es: ¿Qué límite compromete más la generalización de estos resultados?

choices.text: Most volunteers were under forty, so older people could not take part.
The volunteers belonged to a small group unlike most of the general population.
The notice appeared in a newsletter, so the survey was not anonymous.

feedback.es: Los corredores voluntarios no representan a la población; que la mayoría fueran menores de cuarenta no significa que se excluyera a los mayores, y el anonimato no se menciona.

origin.text: The survey was completed by 180 volunteers who answered a notice in a running club's newsletter. Most were under forty, and nearly all reported that they slept well.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud del hablante ante la relación que describe.

choices.text: Doubtful of the link, because only one year group was surveyed.
Convinced that the school's start time explains the whole pattern.
Interested in the link, but careful not to claim too much.

feedback.es: Presenta el dato como un patrón «worth testing, not a rule»: le interesa, pero evita afirmar de más; ni lo descarta por la muestra ni atribuye todo a la hora de entrada.

origin.audio: Our findings are clear on one point: pupils who sleep under seven hours are twice as likely to arrive late. That said, we surveyed only one year group, and the school's start time may matter more than sleep itself. We would therefore treat the link as a pattern worth testing, not as a rule.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las cifras parecen mostrar que las chicas se sienten más cansadas.»

feedback.es: Appear to + verbo base es una forma cauta de presentar lo que muestran los datos.

origin.text: The figures ___ to show that girls feel more tired than boys, but the gap is small and only one school took part.

prompt.es: Redacta los hallazgos y los límites de la encuesta sobre el sueño.

answer.text: Our survey of two hundred pupils produced two main findings. First, sixty per cent of the pupils sleep less than eight hours a night. Second, among those who sleep little, twice as many girls as boys say that they feel tired in class. These figures suggest that a lack of sleep may affect how pupils feel at school, and they appear to show that girls are more affected than boys, at least to some extent. However, the results have an important limitation. All the pupils came from one school, and they described their own sleep, so the data may not be reliable. For this reason, we cannot say that sleep causes tiredness; we can only say that the two seem to be linked. Further research with a larger sample from several schools would be needed before anyone could generalise these results to all teenagers. We therefore treat them as a starting point, not as proof. In short, the findings stand out and deserve attention, but they should be read with caution.
accepted: Our survey of two hundred pupils produced two main findings. First, sixty per cent of the pupils sleep less than eight hours a night. Second, among those who sleep little, twice as many girls as boys say that they feel tired in class. These figures suggest that a lack of sleep may affect how pupils feel at school, and they appear to show that girls are more affected than boys, at least to some extent. However, the results have an important limitation. All the pupils came from one school, and they described their own sleep, so the data may not be reliable. For this reason, we cannot say that sleep causes tiredness; we can only say that the two seem to be linked. Further research with a larger sample from several schools would be needed before anyone could generalise these results to all teenagers. We therefore treat them as a starting point, not as proof. In short, the findings stand out and deserve attention, but they should be read with caution.

We asked two hundred pupils about their sleep and found two things that stand out. To begin with, 60 per cent of them sleep for less than eight hours a night. In addition, among the pupils who sleep little, double the number of girls compared with boys reported feeling tired during lessons. The data indicate that a lack of sleep could affect how pupils feel at school, and girls seem to be more affected than boys to some extent. Nevertheless, there is a key limitation: only one school took part, and the pupils reported their own hours, so the answers may not be reliable. Because of this, the results do not show that sleep causes tiredness; they only point to a link. Further research with a larger sample from different schools would help us to see whether the same pattern appears elsewhere, and whether anyone can generalise from it. We therefore see them as a starting point, not as proof. To sum up, the findings are useful, but they must be treated with caution.

feedback.es: El informe presenta dos hallazgos con cifras, los interpreta con un verbo cauto, explica un límite y propone más investigación.

origin.text: Encuesta sobre el sueño (200 alumnos de un solo colegio, datos declarados por ellos): 120 alumnos (60 %) duermen menos de ocho horas. Entre los que duermen poco, 40 chicas y 20 chicos dicen sentirse cansados en clase (el doble de chicas que de chicos). Escribe unas 170–250 palabras en inglés: dos hallazgos cuantificados, un verbo cauto, un límite explicado y un paso siguiente.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestran los autores ante la necesidad de más pruebas?

choices.text: Impatient: they see no need for further evidence before changing the timetable.
Cautious: they accept that the timetable should change only after repeat studies.
Doubtful: they think their own data may be too unreliable to act on.

feedback.es: Admiten un límite, pero concluyen que el patrón es «obvious» y no ven motivo para esperar («no reason to wait for further evidence»): consideran innecesarias más pruebas antes de actuar.

origin.text: Results. Our survey of 240 pupils at a single school found that 62 per cent sleep under eight hours a night. Among these, 58 pupils reported low marks, compared with 21 of those who sleep longer. We conclude that lack of sleep lowers marks and that every school should start an hour later. Admittedly, all the data were reported by the pupils themselves, and no teacher confirmed the marks. Nevertheless, the pattern is obvious, and we see no reason to wait for further evidence before changing the timetable, since any delay would only harm more pupils.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los hallazgos deben leerse con cautela y nadie debería generalizar.»

feedback.es: Read with caution es la fórmula habitual cuando los datos tienen límites claros.

origin.text: All 240 pupils came from one school and described their own sleep. The findings should therefore be read with ___, and nobody should generalise from them.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué no se puede aislar el efecto del sueño.

choices.text: Only a few schools took part in the trials.
Those schools changed other things at the same time.
The pupils did not report how long they slept.

feedback.es: Los colegios cambiaron también horarios y personal, así que no se sabe qué produjo la mejora.

origin.audio: When the reporter asked whether later starts would raise marks, the researcher replied that the evidence pointed that way but could not prove it. Some schools that moved their start time saw results improve, yet those schools also changed timetables and staff, so the effect of sleep could not be separated out. She said she would be happy to see more trials before anyone calls the question settled.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre un patrón muy claro en una sola escuela?

choices.text: That surveys of single schools are simply never worth doing.
That careful design is enough to make one survey conclusive.
That a striking result in one place may not appear elsewhere.

feedback.es: Sugiere que un patrón visto en un solo lugar puede desaparecer al repetirlo; no descalifica las encuestas de una escuela ni cree que el cuidado del diseño las vuelva concluyentes.

origin.text: Some will say that a pattern this clear needs no further study. I disagree. Clear patterns have a habit of disappearing when somebody repeats the work in a different place, and a survey of one school, however carefully done, is a single observation.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sin embargo, todos los alumnos procedían de una sola escuela.»

answer.text: However all the pupils came from one school

feedback.es: However abre la frase del límite y el resto describe por qué la muestra es limitada.

prompt.es: Completa: «Son demasiado pocos para poder generalizar a partir de ellos.»

feedback.es: Too few to generalise from: una muestra tan pequeña no permite extender lo hallado al resto.

origin.text: Only eleven pupils answered the questionnaire, which is far too few to ___ from: whatever their answers show, they say nothing reliable about the whole school.
